entry_lifecycle.catalyst_logic: The edge is the extreme cross location versus a 3.5-percentile NZDUSD that mixes in the dollar; it is exhausted if AUDNZD holds a new high through 1.2456 or if a New Zealand cash or policy gap starts paying Australia as hard as the listed Australia-Canada cash wedge.
entry_lifecycle.realization_logic: AUDNZD pays if the 99.6 five-year richness fades over weeks as New Zealand cheapness is expressed against Australia rather than against the dollar, not as a two-to-three-day mean-reversion spike.

entry_rationale: Initiate from a flat book a 20 million short in AUDNZD at 1.2456 to own Australia-versus-New Zealand richness at a 99.6 five-year percentile without a dollar leg.
entry_thesis: Australian dollar versus New Zealand dollar at 1.2456 is a 99.6 five-year percentile while the kiwi versus the dollar at 0.5627 is a 3.5 five-year percentile, so the dollar pair mixes New Zealand cheapness with a United States leg and the cross is the cleaner Australia-versus-New Zealand expression. Australian dollar-Canada at 0.9793 is only a 90th percentile, cash Australia 4.60 versus Canada 2.55 still pays 205 basis points to Australia, and Brent 104.77 supports Canada on oil without a new Australia-Canada policy gap. Short the Australia-New Zealand cross from a flat book.

events.rationale: Initiate from a flat book a 20 million short in AUDNZD at 1.2456 to own Australia-versus-New Zealand richness at a 99.6 five-year percentile without a dollar leg.

invalidation: The short is wrong if Australian dollar-New Zealand holds a new high through 1.2456, or if New Zealand cheapness is only a dollar bounce and the kiwi rises while the cross stays rich.
